name: product-tour
title: Product Tour
description: A guided tour that highlights parts of the page one step at a time, with a popover, progress and keyboard navigation, as a React hook and component over driver.js.
author: Kamran Ahmed <https://github.com/kamranahmedse>
docs:
Installed `ProductTour` and `useProductTour` (`@/components/ui/product-tour`), a React wrapper over [driver.js](https://github.com/nilbuild/driver.js) 1.9.0. Its stylesheet is injected once when the hook mounts, so there is no CSS file to import.

Start a tour from a button, so focus returns to it when the tour ends:

```tsx
import { useProductTour } from "@/components/ui/product-tour";

const tour = useProductTour({
  showProgress: true,
  steps: [
    { element: "#search", popover: { title: "Search", description: "Find anything from here." } },
    { element: newButtonRef, popover: { title: "New", description: "Start a project.", side: "bottom", align: "end" } },
    { popover: { title: "All set", description: "A step without an element is centered." } },
  ],
});

<button type="button" onClick={() => tour.start()}>Take the tour</button>
```

Or control it: `<ProductTour open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} steps={steps} />`.

The hook returns `start(index?)`, `stop()`, `moveNext()`, `movePrevious()`, `moveTo(index)`, `active`, `stepIndex` and `getDriver()`. Every driver.js option and hook passes through. Steps are read when the tour starts; unmounting ends the tour without calling back.

Titles, descriptions and button texts are set as HTML by driver.js: never pass untrusted text. The injected `<style>` needs `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` (or a nonce policy that allows it) under a strict Content Security Policy.

Theme it with the `--product-tour-*` variables (popover, popover-foreground, muted-foreground, close, button, button-hover, button-border, shadow, overlay, ring, and `--product-tour-font`); their defaults are driver.js's look. Wraps driver.js by Kamran Ahmed (MIT); the license notice is at the end of the file.
